title: One-Arm Incline Dumbbell Front Raise
overview: The one-arm dumbbell front raise on an incline bench is ashoulder exerciseused to target the front deltoids.The front deltoid is involved in several pressing movements and working to increase the strength of this muscle group can have a positive carry-over into your heavy pushing lifts.Performing unilateral movements can help improve weaknesses, balance your strength and aesthetic physique, and work towards reducing injuries by addressing imbalances in the body.From an aesthetic standpoint, bigger front deltoids can lead to the appearance of a complete set of shoulders and a wider framed upper body.
instructions: Grab a dumbbell and sit on the end of a bench while maintaining a straight back.
Inhale, brace your abs and raise your arm vertically while holding the dumbbell with a pronated grip. Keep a slight bend in your elbow.
Once your arm is parallel with the floor, slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, and then repeat on the other arm.
tips: Practice good form by using a lighter weight.
Don’t lean back as you raise your arms, keep the motion under control, and don’t rely on momentum.
Try not to bounce at the top of the movement, allow the shoulders to flex and then lower slowly.
